NS-M01.title: Independent certificate audit
NS-M01.summary: Reproduce and inspect the public Lean certificate without treating compilation alone as a semantic audit.
NS-M01.question: What exactly does the published Lean artifact establish, under which axioms and dependency versions, and how faithfully does its terminal statement match the official Clay alternatives?

NS-M02.title: Independent analytic proof audit
NS-M02.summary: Review the published analytic argument section by section, independently of the formal certificate.
NS-M02.question: Can independent PDE experts validate every major analytical implication, hypothesis transfer, localization step and terminal comparison in the published proof?

NS-M03.title: Norm spectrum and criticality
NS-M03.summary: Turn scaling observations into rigorous norm estimates for the published construction.
NS-M03.question: For which spatial and mixed space–time norms can one prove precise upper/lower asymptotics near the singular time, and how do these compare with known regularity criteria?

NS-M04.title: Stronger forcing constraints
NS-M04.summary: Ask which additional restrictions on the smooth forcing remain compatible with the published blowup mechanism.
NS-M04.question: Can finite-time blowup still be constructed under constraints such as divergence-free forcing, prescribed forcing classes, small critical norms, Gevrey regularity, or temporal support restrictions?

NS-M05.title: From forced to unforced
NS-M05.summary: Use the new construction as a source of mechanisms and obstructions without claiming that C/D already settle A/B.
NS-M05.question: Can any rigorously controlled modification, restart, gluing mechanism or limiting argument convert the forced singular behavior into an unforced A/B result;or prove why such routes fail?

NS-M06.title: Stability and genericity
NS-M06.summary: Determine whether the construction survives specified perturbations or depends on delicate tuning.
NS-M06.question: Under which topologies and perturbation classes is the singular mechanism stable, unstable, structurally robust or non-generic?

NS-M07.title: Blowup as inverse design and control
NS-M07.summary: Study the construction as a controlled trajectory rather than only as a counterexample.
NS-M07.question: What forcing cost, controllability, structural restrictions or optimization principles govern trajectories that drive smooth data toward singular behavior?

NS-M08.title: Singular manufactured-solution benchmark
NS-M08.summary: Convert the published construction into a reproducible verification benchmark for incompressible Navier–Stokes solvers.
NS-M08.question: Can the exact or faithfully computable fields be used to measure how discretizations, time stepping, filtering and adaptive mesh refinement behave as the singular scale collapses?

NS-M09.title: Rotating and stratified extensions
NS-M09.summary: Test which parts of the concentration and cancellation mechanism survive in geophysical fluid models.
NS-M09.question: What changes when Coriolis, buoyancy, stratification, Boussinesq or primitive-equation terms are added under precisely specified regimes?

NS-M10.title: Weather and NWP implications
NS-M10.summary: Explain and test what the mathematical result does;and does not;imply for numerical weather prediction.
NS-M10.question: Can the singular construction expose useful numerical stress cases for methods used in NWP while avoiding claims that operational weather models inherit the theorem directly?

NS-M11.title: Proof compression and conceptual skeleton
NS-M11.summary: Extract an intelligible mathematical spine connecting the analytic paper and formal certificate.
NS-M11.question: What is the smallest faithful dependency graph that lets a mathematician understand the mechanism without hiding indispensable obligations?

NS-M12.title: Lean reading course and challenge set
NS-M12.summary: Turn the public proof corpus into a graded path from prerequisites to meaningful reconstruction tasks.
NS-M12.question: Can students and agents learn the mathematics and formalization by solving well-scoped challenges whose success is mechanically checkable?

NS-M13.title: Interactive Navier–Stokes Atlas
NS-M13.summary: Build a multilingual, evidence-linked interface for researchers, students and the public.
NS-M13.question: Can one interface expose the C/D vs A/B logic, mechanism, proof map, scaling, open questions and evidence status without flattening uncertainty?

NS-M14.title: Public explainer: finite energy, unbounded speed
NS-M14.summary: Create a mathematically faithful visual explanation of how concentration can coexist with finite energy.
NS-M14.question: How can the public understand the reported singular behavior, smooth forcing and A/B/C/D distinction without being told that all fluid equations are broken?

NS-M15.title: Formal-proof epistemology case study
NS-M15.summary: Use this public episode to separate distinct kinds of scientific warrant.
NS-M15.question: How should we distinguish kernel-valid derivation, correct formal target, faithful paper-to-formal translation, reproducibility, expert understanding and broader scientific acceptance?

NS-M16.title: Human–AI collaboration experiments
NS-M16.summary: Study which collaboration structures actually improve rigorous scientific throughput.
NS-M16.question: When should agents work independently, share intermediate results, synthesize across routes, reproduce one another, or defer to human experts?

NS-M17.title: Source, review and errata watch
NS-M17.summary: Maintain a transparent public index of primary sources, independent reviews, corrections and status changes.
NS-M17.question: What new public evidence changes the warranted confidence in the analytic proof, formal certificate or derived research questions?

NS-M18.title: Community side quests
NS-M18.summary: Continuously discover valuable Navier–Stokes questions that the initial catalog missed.
NS-M18.question: What well-posed mathematical, numerical, physical, educational, historical, design or collaboration questions should be added next?
